summary.text: JB Pritzker, a Democrat, is the 43rd Governor of Illinois and won a third term on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.

A businessman before entering office, he was first elected in 2018 and re-elected in 2022. As governor he signed a phase-in of a $15 minimum wage, an assault-weapons ban, abortion-rights and immigrant-protection laws, and created a Department of Early Childhood.

paragraphs.text: Pritzker graduated from Duke University in 1987 and earned a law degree from Northwestern University.
After college he worked in Washington on the staffs of Rep. Tom Lantos and Sen. Alan Dixon.
He later co-founded Pritzker Group Private Capital with his brother Anthony and served as its managing partner until 2017.
Pritzker won the governorship in 2018 by defeating incumbent Republican Bruce Rauner, and won a second term in 2022 against Darren Bailey.
On June 26, 2025, he announced that he would seek a third term, with former state Rep. Christian Mitchell as his running mate; Bailey was again his Republican opponent.
He and his wife, MK, have been married for more than 30 years and have two children.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election for Governor of Illinois with 60.1% of the vote to Darren Bailey's 36.6% and Collin Corbett's 3.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
